title: ProgramKit bounded corrective reconstruction
intent: Separate human semantics, deterministic ProgramKit structure, and declared authored logic seams; compose existing version/migration/generation/package/quality contracts into a human-reviewed corrective and clean-room reconstruction workflow with honest cross-model evidence.
scope: One accepted-source manifest with exact per-file ownership and edit mode.
Analyzer and build-policy revisions represented in the existing version topology and reverse closure.
A human-reviewed corrective decision composed from existing migration dispositions/actions plus only missing repair and logic-reimplementation actions.
Clean-room reconstruction from an empty application workspace using exact local packages and controlled source mapping.
Separate deterministic structural, logic-seam, package-closure, final-tree, test, and conformance evidence.
Cross-model and review-surface evidence without line-count or behavioral-equivalence overclaim.
nonGoals: Implementation, automatic repair, rollback, history rewriting, provider adapters/bindings/capabilities, autonomous behavior, or a second dependency graph under design approval.
Automatic reconstruction of production data, infrastructure, secrets, operational history, deployment, release, or package-feed publication.
ProgramKit project references, source/file includes, assembly hint paths, or build-output coupling in reconstructed consumers.
assumptions: Existing architecture/design/plan/approval, artifact, generation receipt, source gate, local package, version map, reverse closure, migration wave/action, and evidence contracts remain canonical foundations.
The current C# source gate remains the generated-header/path/build-policy baseline and can be versioned as an implementation/policy node without a parallel topology.
Clean-room application workspaces are newly created and empty; repository history is preserved but is not executable reconstruction input.
Model-authored logic is acceptable only in exact declared editable seams and must pass the same human-reviewed contracts and tests as human-authored logic.

unresolvedDecisions.question: Does semantic inspection at PKCR-W030 confirm that no existing migration action exactly represents implementation repair or declared-logic reimplementation?
unresolvedDecisions.decisionNeededBy: Before any MigrationRequiredAction value or schema is changed in PKCR-W030.
unresolvedDecisions.blockingEffect: If an existing action is semantically exact it must be reused; if neither new action is still needed, the plan stops for material-deviation review.

sourceTruthAuthorities.governs: Ownership classes, accepted source set, topology composition, human decision, reconstruction evidence, cross-model honesty, package boundary, exclusions, and approval boundary.
Current generated header/path, analyzer, build, suppression, receipt, and project-owned source behavior.
The existing node/edge topology consumed by reverse migration closure.
Existing human-reviewed impacted-node disposition and required-action composition.
Current committed output path, digest, and size evidence after atomic generation.
Exact selected local ProgramKit package construction and archive verification.

domains.purpose: Own exact implementation-ownership declarations, human corrective decisions, clean-room application reconstruction, and honest conformance evidence without owning production state or autonomous behavior.

vocabulary.meaning: The finite digest-bound human semantics, generation inputs, declared logic, package/version locks, topology, decisions, policies, and non-secret configuration sufficient for clean-room application reconstruction.
One exact file classified as human-semantic, program-kit-generated, or declared-logic-seam with protected, regenerated, or editable mode.
A human-decided sequence of existing migration actions plus bounded repair or declared-logic reimplementation, followed by package-only clean-room reconstruction and evidence.
The digest of deterministic protected/generated application structure, measured separately from authored logic source and final workspace identity.

semanticModels.meaning: Finite exact source entries, ownership/mode, owner, applicable requirement/logic contract, quality policy, generator/package provenance, and accepted digests.
semanticModels.invariants: Normalized paths are exact and non-overlapping; every materialized source file is declared; protected bytes are unchanged; generated bytes have exact generator/receipt/header/path; editable logic stays inside declared seams.

semanticModels.meaning: Separate digest and evidence bindings for accepted inputs, package closure, version decision, generated structure, human semantics, authored logic, final tree, build/analyzers/tests, ownership conformance, and empty-workspace proof.
semanticModels.invariants: A receipt is emitted only after committed outputs and all required checks pass; it never merges structural identity with logic identity or overstates behavioral equivalence.

semanticModels.meaning: Artifact identities, ownership classes, causal version paths, human dispositions/actions, affected contracts/seams/config/packages, tests, evidence, and unresolved risks prepared for human review.
semanticModels.invariants: Line counts are never correctness, risk, complexity, or equivalence claims; every summary fact resolves to exact artifact or evidence identity.

components.purpose: Provide accepted-source and reconstruction-receipt schemas, models, validation, canonical serialization, and compatibility.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Three ownership classes, three edit modes, exact path/digest semantics, artifact bindings, receipt evidence partitions, and explicit migrations.

components.purpose: Compose accepted-source ownership with the current C# generated-header/path, analyzer, build, no-suppression, package, and generation-receipt gates.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Exact ownership path coverage, generated header/path/profile, declared logic seams, analyzer/build policy identities, diagnostics, and no undeclared outputs.

components.purpose: Compose existing version topology, reverse closure, migration dispositions/actions, and explicit human decision into one bounded corrective assessment.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Existing topology/closure/dispositions/actions plus only RepairImplementation and ReimplementDeclaredLogic if no existing semantic equivalent.

components.purpose: Reconstruct one application in an empty workspace from exact accepted sources and packages after a complete human decision, then emit partitioned evidence.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Empty workspace, accepted source set, exact package closure/source mapping, generation order, ownership gates, selected tests, atomic outputs, and receipt schema.

components.purpose: Compare isolated reconstructions at structural, ownership, seam-contract, test, and evidence boundaries without claiming identical logic or unproved behavioral equivalence.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Identical accepted input, isolated empty workspaces, structural-tree identity, no drift, separate logic digests, shared exact test set, and claim limitations.

referenceRules.referencedScope: ProgramKit projects, source/file includes, assembly hint paths, ProgramKit build outputs, or an uncontrolled first-party package source
referenceRules.rationale: The proof must reconstruct as an external package consumer rather than depend on the ProgramKit build graph.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Corrective assessment, reconstruction operation, fixtures, and evidence
referenceRules.referencedScope: Production data, infrastructure, secrets, operational history, deployment, release, feed publication, provider bindings, development capabilities, or autonomous behavior
referenceRules.rationale: Application source reconstruction is distinct from restoring operational or production state and grants no agent authority.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent implementation ownership, topology participation, human corrective decisions, clean-room reconstruction, cross-model conformance, evidence partitions, and exclusions as one validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no repair, reconstruction, migration, rollback, or autonomous behavior.

valueLifecycle.rationale: Exact bytes are validated, digest-bound by the plan and review manifest, and compared during approved work-unit closure.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set and accepted source set are explicit inputs; no retrieval system is created.

agentProcedure.rationale: This design creates no capability, provider binding, MCP server, skill, or autonomous procedure.

humanCommunication.audience: The human ProgramKit reviewer, corrective-decision owner, and later bounded implementer.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of this review-set version and exact canonical design and plan SHA-256 values authorizes implementation; each reconstruction also requires a complete human migration decision.
humanCommunication.rationale: The Markdown projection, fixtures, validation report, and manifest expose exact ownership, decision, proof, claim, and exclusion boundaries.

governance.provenancePolicy: Exact human intent and ProgramKit b4b14cd source gate, version map, migration, receipt, ownership, local-package, and source-map bytes are named; implementation cannot become retroactive design authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and plan bind exact canonical bytes; material changes require revalidation, new digests, and renewed human approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Ownership classes/modes, exact path coverage, topology edges, migration action additions, accepted input set, package boundary, reconstruction order, receipt partitions, cross-model tests, and claim limitations version independently.
governance.migrationPolicy: Existing version map, reverse closure, migration dispositions/actions, waves, and evidence are composed; schema/action changes require explicit revision/migration; every impacted node requires a human disposition before execution.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Accepted sources and receipts exclude secret values, production data, operational records, credentials, and deployment state.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Canonical technical documentation and evidence remain in ProgramKit or the owning reconstruction/tool repository; projections cannot become authority.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Temporary workspaces, processes, model conversations, and runtime state are not canonical inputs and are destroyed only through bounded verified fixture cleanup.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A schema-governed design composes current ProgramKit foundations while implementation, corrective execution, and autonomous behavior remain blocked.

security.policy: Accepted inputs are exact, non-secret, package-mapped, and path-contained; undeclared or ambient inputs fail closed.
guarantees: No production data, secrets, credentials, infrastructure, or operational history is accepted.
All materialized paths remain inside the new application workspace.
ProgramKit is consumed through exact local packages only.
exclusions: Reconstruction is not production recovery or deployment.

authority.policy: Humans own semantics, approval, and each impacted-node disposition/action; ProgramKit generates deterministic structure and models/humans author only declared logic seams.
guarantees: No corrective action executes before a complete reviewed decision.
No model may edit protected or generated structure.
No automatic rollback or history rewrite occurs.
exclusions: A recommendation, reverse closure, or passing test is not authority to migrate, repair, or release.

secrets.policy: Only non-secret configuration templates and secret reference names may be accepted; values remain provider/operations-owned.
guarantees: Receipts and fixtures contain no secret values.
exclusions: Secret reconstruction or migration is prohibited.

persistence.policy: Exact accepted inputs, committed source outputs, ordinary version-control history, and bounded evidence persist.
guarantees: Receipts are emitted only after output commit and verification.
History remains preserved without becoming required executable input.
exclusions: Build outputs, temporary workspaces, and runtime/operational state are not accepted source.

failure.policy: Missing/overlapping ownership, undeclared paths, structural drift, incomplete decisions, package drift, failed analyzers/tests, or receipt mismatch fail without partial success claims.
guarantees: No failed reconstruction is reported as clean-room proof.
exclusions: Failure does not trigger rollback, history rewrite, or compensating production action.

concurrency.policy: One reconstruction owns one empty workspace and receipt; parallel model fixtures use isolated roots and immutable common inputs.
guarantees: No shared mutable generated-output or package-lock state exists between fixtures.
exclusions: Concurrent writes to one application workspace are prohibited.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation stops remaining stages, leaves no success receipt, and preserves accepted inputs and version history.
guarantees: Atomic generation and path containment prevent committed partial generated files from becoming success evidence.
exclusions: Cancellation does not imply rollback of external or production state because such state is out of scope.

observability.policy: Evidence partitions accepted inputs, causal closure/decision, package closure, generated structure, human semantics, logic source, final tree, build/analyzers/tests, and ownership conformance.
guarantees: Cross-model evidence records distinct logic digests and exact shared tests.
Review surfaces resolve to artifact identities and causal paths.
exclusions: Line counts and identical generated output do not become correctness or equivalence claims.

compatibility.policy: Ownership/source/receipt schemas, analyzer/build-policy nodes, migration actions, package closure, generator/output identities, and test contracts version independently through the existing topology.
guarantees: Analyzer or build-policy change reaches consumers through reverse closure.
Existing dispositions/actions are reused where semantically exact.
Generated structural identity and authored logic identity remain separate.
exclusions: No universal cross-model behavioral equivalence is claimed.

scenarios.intent: Choose an exact corrective disposition and actions for every node reached by reverse closure.
preconditions: Version map includes exact analyzer/build-policy nodes and dependency paths.
Current and target component versions and compatibility evidence validate.
steps: Compute reverse fixed-point closure and causal paths.
Present unchanged-with-proof, compatible actions, redesign, manual review, and blocked choices.
Bind each impacted node to one human disposition and exact actions.
Refuse execution while any node is undecided or blocked.
outcomes: The complete assessment is digest-bound input to reconstruction.
Only semantically missing repair and declared-logic actions extend the existing vocabulary.
failureOutcomes: The workflow never infers approval or silently selects an action.

scenarios.intent: Reconstruct a package-only application from the exact accepted source set in an empty workspace.
preconditions: Design/plan/approval, accepted source, package closure, topology/decision, generators, and policies validate.
The application workspace is newly created, empty, and path-contained.
steps: Prepare exact local ProgramKit packages and controlled NuGet source mapping.
Materialize protected human semantics, generate deterministic structure, and materialize only accepted logic-seam source.
Restore/build locked, run ownership/source gates and selected tests, and commit outputs atomically.
outcomes: Repeated exact inputs yield byte-identical generated/protected structural output.
No structural drift, undeclared source, or ProgramKit build coupling exists.
failureOutcomes: Any non-empty workspace, digest drift, ownership violation, package leak, analyzer/test failure, or incomplete decision prevents a success receipt.

scenarios.intent: Compare two isolated authored-logic reconstructions honestly.
preconditions: Both sessions receive identical accepted inputs and isolated empty workspaces.
Both may edit only identical declared logic seams.
steps: Run both reconstructions with the same exact packages, generators, policies, contracts, property tests, and negative tests.
Compare structural-tree identity and ownership drift.
Record separate logic-tree and final-tree digests and exact shared test outcomes.
Present bounded claims and unresolved risks without line-count metrics.
outcomes: Generated/protected structure is identical and authored logic remains visibly distinct where it differs.
Only behaviors covered by the exact shared contracts/tests receive evidence.
failureOutcomes: Passing tests never becomes a general behavioral-equivalence claim.

statusClaims.claim: The review design exists from explicit human intent; no ownership contract, policy change, corrective action, reconstruction operation, provider integration, or runtime behavior is implemented or approved.
